plus the SPEC 4.3 WebSocket, with the real clock, so the escalation arc can be
rehearsed exactly as it will play on stage:
t=2.1s   provisional answer + groundedness verdict + job_id  (turn ENDS here)

turn.question: When did the van arrive at the loading door?
turn.provisional_answer: A white panel van reverses toward the loading door starting at 21:11:07 and is stopped across the fire door bay by 21:11:11. It has not moved again through 21:11:52.

turn.question: Was the van's rear door open when it backed up?
turn.provisional_answer: A white panel van reversed toward the loading door around 21:11. The caption doesn't record whether its rear door was open.

job.question: Was the van's rear door open when it backed up?
job.answer: Yes. The rear doors are open from 21:11:19 onward - visible as the van turns. Two figures approach from the right at 21:11:41.
job.reasoning: Re-decoded 45 s at native resolution, 4 fps (181 frames). Frames up to 21:11:18 show the van at an angle with the rear face occluded by the door pillar, which is why the 1 fps live caption could not commit either way. At 21:11:19 the van yaws roughly 15 degrees and both rear doors are visible, swung outward past the body line; the left door edge casts a shadow onto the loading apron that tracks with the door, not the body, confirming it is open rather than a reflection. The doors remain open in every subsequent frame. At 21:11:41 two figures enter from the right edge and reach the rear of the van by 21:11:47. No cargo movement is visible within the analysed range.

turn.question: Why did you alert at 21:11?
turn.provisional_answer: read_action_log(21:00-22:00) returns act-0001: raise_alert on fire-door-blocked at 21:11:14, fired on stage-2 confidence after a 120 s sustain. act-0002 amended it to verified at 21:11:52 with a clip attached. The later alert at 21:34:02 was retracted - the worker found headlight glare, not a vehicle.
